mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with a partial offset from residential construction, resulting in muted but positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from a positive threshold of +0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which erodes real corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from a positive threshold of +0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 YoY change), signals a shift from spending to saving that foreshadows weaker consumer demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA AND GDPC1 YoY change < 0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase of at least 0.4% in both the industrial production index (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based acceleration in supply-side activity, which raises earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.4% AND HOUST monthly change > 0.4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.
